chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: The Link mouthpiece for tenor soloists
summary: Tenor men used Link mouthpieces to cut above the brass, while altos mostly stayed with rubber ones.

blocks.x: Did any of the reed men
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Most of them all used the Link. We used to use the Link.
And they were all at that time rubber.

Whatchamacallem used that mouthpiece I was trying to tell you about now. He used a rubber mouthpiece. It was a very good mouthpiece. But the rubber mouthpiece -- the Link was mostly for the tenor men that had to do a lot of honking. You know, playing really. You know, that was a good mouthpiece for them. But most your alto players, some of them use a Link (inaudible), most of them use rubber mouthpieces, because they were used to that (inaudible). See, alto players didn't have to do what the tenor players had to do. He had to play above the crowd -- above that brass all the time. He was a soloist. You got to -- (inaudible) they got blow, you know. They expect you to blow, you know.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

(Inaudible) Hamp doing "Flying Home", or something, you know -- One O'Clock Jump, you come in you got to blow, you know. Give him something (Inaudible) with some power that you can push. So that's why the soloist (inaudible). Hot tenor players in the bands use the Link, and things like that. Gave them a lot of carrying power, you know, to get above that brass. Like I say, when the brass is falling behind you be playing something, that brass be hitting those big ones (inaudible) behind you. You got to be able, you know, try to get out there above all that noise. You be playing in a mike too, but it still helps you, you know that hipper (inaudible) sound.
